sections.title: 2026 Mexican City Grand Prix
sections.sections_content:
It's been a stop-start journey for the Mexican City Grand Prix. Originally first held in 1962, it only ran through to 1970. It made a comeback in 1986 but again only ran through to 1992.

After a twelve-year absence, the Mexican City GP returned to the F1 calendar in 2015. Originally thought to run through just 2019, it was later announced that the race would be in place until at least 2025.

The track is unique, it's 2 km above sea level and also passes through a baseball stadium!

How long is the Mexican City Grand Prix?

The lap at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is fairly short, just 4.3 km (2.6 miles), meaning we get a total of 71 laps during the GP.

Mexico City Grand Prix

When is the Mexican City Grand Prix?

  • Friday 30th October - Practice 1 & 2
  • Saturday 31st October - Practice 3 & Qualifying
  • Sunday 1st November - The Race

Where can I watch the Mexican City Grand Prix?

As with all F1 races this season, you can watch it live on the Sky Sports F1 channel or catch up with the highlights on Channel 4.

Alternatively, if you fancy a trip to Mexico, then book those tickets! Situated in Mexico City, you can mix the vibrant city life with the racing.

sections.title: Past Winners & Fastest Laps
sections.sections_content:
Who has won the Mexican City Grand Prix?

The only active drivers who have recorded multiple wins are Max Verstappen, who has five wins to his name, and Lewis Hamilton, who won it in 2016 & 2019.

Red Bull leads the way for constructor wins with five, one behind are McLaren with four wins, whilst Ferrari, Mercedes and Williams have won the GP on three occasions each.

The official fastest lap holder at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is Valtteri Bottas, who set a time of 1:17.774 during the 2021 Mexico City Grand Prix.

What does Pole produce at the Mexico City Grand Prix?

Winning Grid Starts (Oldest to Lastest): 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 1, 3, 1, 1

From the last 10 Mexico City Grand Prix, a total of 5 drivers have won from pole, which is a success rate of 50% for drivers turning pole into a win. When looking at those who have started on the front row, then that number is 70% (7-10) of the race wins have come from the front row.

The Fate of Pole Sitters (Oldest to Lastest): 1, 1, 4, Ret, 4, 15, 1, 3, 1, 1

Looking at the finishing positions of the pole sitters, then 60% (6-10) of them have finished on the podium.

Previous Mexico City Grand Prix Winners

Here are the last 10 winners of the Mexico City Grand Prix:

  • 2025: Lando Norris (McLaren)
  • 2024: Carlos Sainz Jr. (Ferrari)
  • 2023: Max Verstappen (Red Bull Racing)
  • 2022: Max Verstappen (Red Bull Racing)
  • 2021: Max Verstappen (Red Bull Racing)
  • 2019: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)
  • 2018: Max Verstappen (Red Bull Racing)
  • 2017: Max Verstappen (Red Bull Racing)
  • 2016: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)
  • 2015: Nico Rosberg (Mercedes)

Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez Fastest Laps

Here at the last 10 fastest laps set at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez:

  • 2025: George Russell (Mercedes)
  • 2024: Charles Leclerc (Ferrari)
  • 2023: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)
  • 2022: George Russell (Mercedes)
  • 2021: Valtteri Bottas (Mercedes)
  • 2019: Charles Leclerc (Ferrari)
  • 2018: Valtteri Bottas (Mercedes)
  • 2017: Sebastian Vettel (Ferrari)
  • 2016: Daniel Ricciardo (Red Bull Racing)
  • 2015: Nico Rosberg (Mercedes)

  • August: Dutch Grand Prix (23rd)

  • October: Singapore Grand Prix (11th), United States Grand Prix (25th)
  • November: Mexico City Grand Prix (1st), São Paulo Grand Prix (8th), Las Vegas Grand Prix (21st), Qatar Grand Prix (29th)
  • December: Abu Dhabi Grand Prix (6th)
